text:
monica (support): FYI customer ThriveChat opened ticket #12345 — they started seeing a sustained 5xx spike around 11:12 UTC. ~20-30% of requests hitting 502/504 from the hosted API. Customer says it started after a sudden traffic burst. link: https://support.redwood.example/t/12345
ingress-bot: observed: gateway.queue_depth per-host: 320/200 (limit), p95 ingress latency jumped 2.3s -> 18s between 11:11-11:14, continuous_batcher backlog count ++++ (see dashboard) https://dashboards.redwood.example/d/queue/ingress
devon (sre): grabbing traces now. initial look: lots of requests stuck in continuous-batcher waiting for prefix aggregation, then queued, then early_rejects/timeout at gateway. I'm seeing repeated re-enqueue attempts for the same tenant id. Can you paste a few request_ids from the ticket?
monica (support): paste from the ticket: req_8a7c2, req_8a7c3, req_8a7c9. Customer provided a repro curl: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"model":"open-xxl","input":"<~8k tokens>","max_tokens":256}'
```
kai (eng-runtime): thanks. two quick asks: 1) run this on prod to dump batcher queue snapshot, 2) if we need a hotfix we can toggle continuous batching per-tenant.
```
kubectl -n prod exec deploy/batcher -- /bin/bash -c "./admin dump-queue --tenant thrivechat --since 20m > /tmp/thrive-queue.log"
curl -sS http://batcher-admin.prod.svc/tenants/thrivechat | jq .batching.enabled
```
devon (sre): running traces + logs. seeing a pattern: long-seq requests (8k tokens) keep triggering large aggregation windows, which increases effective wait time for short requests getting batched behind them. The batcher accumulates N-heavy requests -> queue depth climbs -> gateway early_rejects when queue_depth > threshold. Also multiple KV-cache misses causing per-request slowdowns.
jenna (customer-success): customer says they ramped from 50rps -> 450rps in ~30s during a scheduled marketing event. They didn't change seq lengths. They expect SLA; can we provide a mitigation asap?
devon (sre): mitigation plan (short): 1) temporarily throttle tenant at ingress to 200rps, 2) disable continuous batching for that tenant so it falls back to immediate dispatch, 3) scale batcher replicas +2 to drain backlog, 4) enable model fallback to a smaller variant for heavy requests. I'll run steps 1-3 now.
```
# throttle
PATCH https://config.redwood.internal/api/tenants/thrivechat -d '{"ingress": {"rate_limit_rps": 200}}'
# disable continuous batching
PATCH https://batcher-admin.prod.svc/tenants/thrivechat -d '{"batching":{"continuous":false}}'
# scale batcher
kubectl -n prod scale deploy/batcher --replicas=6
```
monica (support): applied throttle + disable continuous batching. ingress-bot: throttle applied for tenant thrivechat: rps=200. batcher replicas scaling started.
ingress-bot: after throttle: queue_depth dropped from 320 -> 85 within 45s, p95 ingress latency down to 3.1s. early_rejects rate decreased.
monica (support): customer reported reduced 5xxs after ~2m. they still see sporadic 502s but much lower.
kai (eng-runtime): digging into root cause: continuous-batching logic favors waiting for tokens to reach a target window; large inputs + high ramp combined with kvcache churn means some in-flight batches take >1500ms to process. That plus queue_depth threshold leads to gateway timeouts. Long-term fixes: - add dynamic batch-window shrink when queue_depth > X - per-tenant batching caps (max aggregate tokens) - smarter kvcache warmup and eviction limits.
devon (sre): filing a post-incident action: runbook update with immediate mitigations (throttle, disable continuous batching, scale replicas, enable fallback), add alert on continuous_batcher.backlog_ms > 800ms for >30s.
jenna (customer-success): I'll update the customer and ask them to moderate the scheduled ramp temporarily; they asked for an ETA for a permanent fix. What's realistic?
kai (eng-runtime): ETA: pragmatic improvements in 2-3 sprints (6-8 weeks) for dynamic window + per-tenant caps. Shorter patch to add a gearbox flag to reduce continuous batch window under high queue pressure could be prioritized in 1 sprint if we agree.
monica (support): marking incident as mitigated for now. saving commands/snippets to ticket. follow-up items: DEV-INC-981 add alert, RUNTIME-PR-264 small-window-under-pressure flag, RUNBOOK-QUEUE update.
monica (support): thanks all :thumbsup:
